source_text: Cumque reticeret, Augustinus episcopus ecclesiae catholicae dixit: Si ergo sub ueritate tacuisti, non sine causa uenisti, nisi quia istos decipere uoluisti. cumque diu reticeret, Augustinus episcopus ecclesiae catholicae dixit: Uidetis, fratres, diu tacentem; moneo ut optetis resipiscentem, obsecro ne sequamini pereuntem. uerumtamen quoniam gesta collationis nostrae commemorauit, ubi apparere posse dixit, utrum ueritate sit uictus an potestate oppressus, multa sunt quidem ubi superfluis et moratoriis proseeutionibus gesta cumularunt, nihil aliud magnis uiribus agentes, nisi ut nihil ageretur; sed domino praesidente et causam suam agente uentum est quo noluerunt. dicta causa atque definita est. sed si omnia gesta uobis legere uelimus, quamquam praesentibus uobis fratrem et coepiscopum meum Deuterium obstringo, ut, quemadmodum fit apud Carthaginem, apud Tagastem, apud Constantinam, apud Hipponem, apud omnes diligentes ecclesias, sic etiam deinceps facere non pigrescat, ut annis omnibus per ieiuniorum dies, id est quadragesima ante pascha, quando uobis maxime ieiunantibus plus uacat audire, eadem gesta collationis per annos singulos uniuersa a capite in finem recitentur ex ordine, tamen, ut dicere coeperam, quia non omnia uobis modo legere possumus, dignamini prius audire ante collationem quas litteras dederimus ad cognitorem, ubi promisimus uel quemadmodum suscipi uellemus si uicti fuissemus, uel quemadmodum eos susciperemus si uinceremus, ut uideretur non in contentione, sed in humilitate esse uictoria.
thought_title: Silence as defeat, and the promise of the conference records
orientation: Augustine is speaking to the gathered congregation in the Catholic church, with Emeritus the Donatist bishop present but refusing to answer.
pass_a_gloss: And while he kept silent, Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: If therefore you kept silent under truth, you did not come without a reason, except because you wanted to deceive these people. And while he kept silent for a long time, Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: You see, brothers, the man silent for a long time; I warn you that you should wish for him to come to his senses, I beg you not to follow him as he perishes. Nevertheless, since he mentioned the records of our conference, where he said it could appear whether he was defeated by truth or crushed by power, there are indeed many places where they piled up the records with superfluous and delaying proceedings, doing nothing else with great efforts except that nothing should be done; but with the Lord presiding and pleading his own cause, it came to what they did not want. The case was pleaded and decided. But if we should wish to read all the records to you, although in your presence I bind my brother and fellow bishop Deuterius, that, as is done at Carthage, at Thagaste, at Constantina, at Hippo, at all diligent churches, so also from now on he should not be slow to do, that in all years through the days of fasting, that is the forty days before Easter, when you especially fasting have more leisure to hear, the same records of the conference should be read through each year, all of them from beginning to end in order, nevertheless, as I had begun to say, because we cannot read all of them to you now, deign first to hear what letter we gave before the conference to the judge, where we promised either in what way we would wish to be received if we had been defeated, or in what way we would receive them if we should win, so that the victory might be seen to be not in contention but in humility.

choices.why: Keeps the literal force of 'sub' with the ablative, meaning under the pressure or weight of truth, matching Augustine's contrast between truth and power.
The participle captures the process of repentance and recovery of right mind that Augustine wishes for Emeritus.
Preserves the legal-technical flavor of 'prosecutio' as a formal procedural step, and 'moratorius' as designed to cause delay.

choices.term: nihil aliud magnis uiribus agentes, nisi ut nihil ageretur
choices.english: doing nothing else with great efforts except that nothing should be done
choices.why: Keeps the paradox of 'doing nothing' with 'great efforts' and the purpose clause exactly, which is the rhetorical point.
rejected: striving mightily so that nothing would happen

choices.why: The verb has a strong legal-moral force of placing under obligation, which fits Augustine's public charge to Deuterius.
The deponent imperative carries a courteous but formal request to the congregation, fitting the public liturgical setting.

pass_b_english: And when he kept silent, Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: If then you kept silent under truth, you did not come without a reason—except that you wanted to deceive these people. And when he kept silent for a long time, Augustine, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: You see, brothers, how long he has been silent. I warn you to wish that he come to his senses; I beg you not to follow him as he perishes.

But since he brought up the records of our conference, where he said it could appear whether he was defeated by truth or crushed by power, there are indeed many places where they piled up the records with superfluous and delaying proceedings, doing nothing else with great efforts except that nothing should be done. But with the Lord presiding and pleading his own cause, it came to the point they did not want. The case was stated and decided.

But if we wanted to read all the records to you—although in your presence I bind my brother and fellow bishop Deuterius, so that just as is done at Carthage, at Thagaste, at Constantina, at Hippo, and in all the churches that care, he should not be slow to do the same from now on: that every year during the days of fasting, that is, the forty days before Easter, when you have the most time to listen because you are fasting, the same records of the conference should be read aloud in full, from beginning to end, in order, each year—nevertheless, as I had begun to say, because we cannot read everything to you now, deign first to hear what letter we sent to the judge before the conference, where we promised both how we would want to be received if we were defeated, and how we would receive them if we won, so that it might be seen that victory lies not in contention but in humility.

problems.quote: I urge you to pray that he comes to his senses
problems.why: optetis means 'wish/desire', not 'pray'; moneo is 'warn/advise', not 'urge'
problems.fix: I warn you to wish that he come to his senses

edits.old: I urge you to pray that he comes to his senses
edits.new: I warn you to wish that he come to his senses

fixed: Changed 'I urge you to pray that he comes to his senses' to 'I warn you to wish that he come to his senses': moneo means 'warn/advise', optetis means 'wish/desire', not 'pray'.

last_rejected.quote: I warn you to wish that he come to his senses
last_rejected.why: "optetis" means "pray for" not "wish"; "resipiscentem" is "one coming to his senses" (participle), not a jussive "that he come."
last_rejected.fix: I urge you to pray for him to come to his senses
last_rejected.ruling: 'optetis' = wish/pray; 'resipiscentem' = one coming to senses. English conveys meaning adequately.

last_rejected.quote: doing nothing else with great efforts except that nothing should be done
last_rejected.source_quote: nihil aliud magnis uiribus agentes, nisi ut nihil ageretur
last_rejected.why: "magnis uiribus agentes" means "using great force/violence," not "great efforts"; they actively obstructed proceedings violently.
last_rejected.fix: using great force to achieve nothing else but that nothing be done
last_rejected.ruling: 'magnis uiribus' can mean 'great efforts/force'; 'great efforts' is within normal range, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: it could appear whether he was defeated by truth or crushed by power
last_rejected.source_quote: utrum ueritate sit uictus an potestate oppressus
last_rejected.why: The subject is Augustine/Emeritus (masculine singular), but "he" is ambiguous; more importantly, "apparere posse dixit" = "he said it could appear/be made clear"—the English loses that Emeritus claimed this could be shown.
last_rejected.fix: where he said it could be made clear whether he was defeated by truth or crushed by power
last_rejected.ruling: 'he said it could appear' is present in English; 'he' subject is clear from context. No major error.
